entries.title: Versioned text-to-avatar serving pipeline
entries.summary: The server resolves questions, retrieves reviewed sources, and invokes a configured dialogue model. It returns answer text, citations and a behavior plan. The browser renders the avatar and controls playback and its clock. This describes the architecture; a specific running installation can use different optional components.

entries.title: Committed corpus versus locally exported interviews
entries.summary: The documented default Jensen Huang corpus contains 32 editorial evidence records from nine dated sources, including 24 paraphrased exchanges. Reviewed workbench exports are separate and an individual runtime can load a different corpus. Retrieval adds evidence to the input without training model weights.

entries.title: Configurable local dialogue model
entries.summary: The setup guide documents a separate OpenAI-compatible dialogue endpoint and a Qwen3-TTS MLX worker. Its example uses a Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 4-bit local text model in one Mac trial. The trial does not establish the team’s model-selection rationale, a ranking against alternatives, or which weights are loaded on the presentation machine.
entries.engineering_rationale_en: a local quantized dialogue model can keep generation on the laptop with a compatible endpoint.
entries.engineering_rationale_ko: 호환되는 로컬 엔드포인트와 연결하면 양자화한 대화 모델을 노트북에서 실행할 수 있습니다.

entries.title: Separate reference-conditioned voice synthesis
entries.summary: The local Qwen3-TTS MLX voice uses an explicit Jensen persona binding and a reviewed recording and transcript. The voice worker verifies the reference hashes. The independent dialogue model produces the text. Reference conditioning does not by itself update model weights.

entries.title: Committed-sentence audio playback
entries.summary: The Qwen MLX path can start synthesizing the first committed English sentence while the language model continues writing. The browser uses one audio clock and adaptive buffering. A standard non-MLX voice provider can instead synthesize a WAV for each committed sentence before PCM delivery. This does not establish venue latency.

entries.title: Configured appearance and gesture assets
entries.summary: The studio documentation separates the Gaussian face bundle, a body or rig, and optional learned gesture bundles. Gaussian face data supplies appearance, FLAME data and recorded expression coefficients; gesture data is selected separately. Private asset files and explicit runtime switches are required. The presence of a renderer or a learned-preview switch is not a measured result for facial likeness, natural gesture quality or semantic expression accuracy.

entries.title: Evidence export and multimodal alignment limits
entries.summary: The audited workbench exports reviewed text exchanges and source metadata to the dialogue corpus. Speech-reference preparation and visual assets have separate inputs and review records. These serving and export paths do not establish that every text passage has a jointly validated matching audio segment and visible speaking-face segment. Describe MCCCD-style utterance alignment as an intended collection approach unless the exact aligned dataset and its review record are supplied.

entries.title: Quality and latency measurement boundaries
entries.summary: The project distinguishes server request timing from browser playback and audible-output latency. Its documented benchmark harness can run real local LLM, speech and application processes with pinned assets. Results from one CPU or cached run do not establish latency on a teammate's Mac or at the venue. The answer should cite an actual run record before reporting any numeric speed improvement or voice-quality gain.

entries.title: Merged optional persona graph and delivery guidance
entries.summary: PR #29 merged into main. It adds optional source-bound persona-value and delivery guidance. A matched Qwen experiment did not show a net gain in strict advice quality. Merging the code does not show that the optional graph is active in the demo or that a separate Sophon session uses it.

entries.title: Merged EMAGE gesture and upper-body Gaussian tooling
entries.summary: PR #27 merged into main. It adds an EMAGE speech-to-gesture preview and upper-body Gaussian tooling. The separate Sophon real-time route does not inherit the Python text/RAG engine. The selected provider and installed assets determine which parts are active in a particular run.

entries.title: Project overview
cues: what is the purpose of this project
entries.summary: The student team built Who Is Your Bias?, a research studio that connects documented statements to a conversational model and synchronized avatar. The active simulated subject is Jensen Huang. An audience member can ask a question, hear an answer when voice is connected, and inspect the sources. The avatar is a simulation and does not speak for NVIDIA.

entries.title: Separate dialogue and voice workers
entries.summary: The dialogue model generates the text and a separate Qwen3-TTS worker renders committed sentences as audio. These services can overlap, use separate checkpoints, and be configured separately.
entries.engineering_rationale_en: separate workers can render a completed sentence while the dialogue model continues composing its reply.
entries.engineering_rationale_ko: 작업자를 분리하면 대화 모델이 답변을 이어 쓰는 동안 확정된 문장을 먼저 합성할 수 있습니다.

entries.title: Documented purpose of early sentence synthesis
entries.summary: The documented path starts synthesis on the first committed English sentence so that it can overlap continued text generation. The browser buffers audio across sentence boundaries. This mechanism does not establish a numeric improvement or model-selection motive.

entries.title: Local Qwen MLX trial
entries.summary: PR #32 (https://github.com/Dindb-dong/who-is-your-bias/pull/32) reports one local Chrome text-input trial with two sentences, a local Qwen LLM and Qwen3-TTS MLX. The first browser audio signal arrived in 5.24 seconds with zero observed queue interruptions. The trial did not measure microphone input or EMAGE.

entries.title: Server and browser responsibilities
entries.summary: The server owns evidence, prompts, provider credentials, bounded conversation state, and behavior plans. Browser responsibilities include microphone interaction, rendering, interruptions, playback and the authoritative audio clock.

entries.title: What live timing measures
entries.summary: Browser first render, browser first audio signal, and server model or PCM events measure different stages. Text-input measurements exclude capture and transcription. Report the clock and setup alongside the number.

entries.title: Microphone and transcription path
entries.summary: The studio can dictate Korean or English with a selected question language. It uses a configured server ASR or supported browser recognizer. Stopping capture finalizes the question. Browser support and permission matter, and typed input is independent.

entries.title: Sentence-aligned Korean captions
entries.summary: In the bilingual text and retrieval path, input, spoken answer, and subtitle languages are separate. Sentence translation runs beside synthesis. The playing audio's PCM offset determines the displayed sentence. This is not word-level alignment.

entries.title: Late translation behavior
entries.summary: The documented caption path gives translation a short deadline after backend audio delivery. Late or failed captions can fall back to labeled English. The browser can still have audio in its queue even when backend delivery is done.

entries.title: What citations can verify
entries.summary: The application checks whether citation markers point to supplied evidence IDs. It does not prove that the evidence supports the exact claim. Semantic answer quality requires separate review.

entries.title: Held-out source isolation
entries.summary: An entire held-out source is excluded from runtime retrieval, including its records and reference answers. This preserves the distinction between available evidence and material used to evaluate generalization.

entries.title: Review of imported transcripts
entries.summary: Locally imported captions are draft records until target-speaker attribution, segmentation, publication information and timebase are reviewed. The reviewed records can enter retrieval. Raw audio, videos and private transcripts are outside the public corpus.

entries.title: Browser camera processing and user selection
entries.summary: The capture path processes face positions in the browser and does not upload, record or persist camera frames. A presenter selects whom the avatar watches. Positional tracking does not establish a person's identity.

entries.title: Eyes lead and the head follows
entries.summary: When the presenter selects a target, the avatar's eyes move first and the head follows after a delay. New positions for the same participant do not restart that transition. This is an animation rule rather than recognition of emotion.

entries.title: Independent avatar window
entries.summary: The studio exposes a separate avatar presentation window while the main browser tab owns conversation controls. This presentation feature does not select a different model. Test actual caption and display behavior on the event setup.

entries.title: Optional Gaussian-head preview
entries.summary: The Gaussian-head preview can composite a learned Jensen head onto a clothed body. The renderer may use labeled recorded or static expression fallback. The default rig remains available. Visual likeness and live expression naturalness require separate evaluation.

entries.title: Head and body geometry preview
entries.summary: The preview documents a collar cut and reference transforms for a Gaussian head on a clothed SMPL-X body. An export or merge does not prove a newly trained upper-body model is running on the presentation machine.

entries.title: Speech-driven motion
entries.summary: Optional EMAGE uses audio to generate SMPL-X motion. The renderer syncs motion to the matching audio and adapts it to the avatar. Its motion follows audio and is not generated from the meaning of each word.

entries.title: Motion timing compromise
entries.summary: Live EMAGE works in overlapping windows, with boundary cross-fades. Shorter windows require less audio before motion starts but change the overlap and visual behavior. The documented measurements are bounded to that setup.

entries.title: Voice reference and learned adaptation
entries.summary: The report compares reference-only conditioning with an artifact after 16 adaptation updates. Evaluation includes example English and Korean audio and diagnostics. The Korean sample does not establish separate Korean training or verified human listening quality.

entries.title: English live voice and Korean language input
entries.summary: The local Qwen MLX live worker is documented for English sentences. Korean questions and Korean captions are separate from the live voice language. An experimental Korean voice sample does not establish a deployed Korean voice.

entries.title: Local OpenAI-compatible interface
entries.summary: Dialogue uses a configured OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Compatibility describes the interface. The endpoint can be a local model, so compatibility alone does not mean the presentation calls OpenAI.

entries.title: Evidence preview without generation
entries.summary: The no-key default returns evidence notes without a generative provider. This demonstrates retrieval, not generation or new persona reasoning. Dialogue and audio providers are separately configured.

entries.title: Adaptive response structure
entries.summary: Optional bilingual patterns can adapt normal-dialogue answer structure and length without a second model call. This is prompting guidance, not a guaranteed shape. Normal dialogue and dedicated project Q&A are separate paths.

entries.title: Public interview delivery guidance
cues: how do you model the persona
entries.summary: Optional observations from interviews inform tone, values and delivery. They do not source team engineering facts. The cited evaluation did not establish a net quality gain for the optional persona graph.

entries.title: Sophon and evidence-grounded dialogue
entries.summary: The cited Python retrieval route and optional Sophon conversation are separate. A project card or persona graph added to Python does not automatically become Sophon context. Verify which route is running.

entries.title: Who built the simulation
entries.summary: The project team built the studio. Jensen Huang is the subject of a labeled AI simulation. Public evidence and speaking-style observations do not imply that Jensen or NVIDIA built, approved, or speaks through the project.

entries.title: How to identify the active demo stack
entries.summary: The repository exposes separately configured model, voice, avatar and gesture options. Only an inspection and end-to-end run of the event installation identify the currently active settings and assets.

entries.title: Interruptions and stale playback
entries.summary: Replacing or resetting a turn invalidates the previous playback generation to prevent late audio from starting in the next conversation. Stopping playback does not guarantee an external synchronous provider stops computing immediately.

entries.title: Mouth cue timing and provenance
entries.summary: The prepared-speech route binds mouth cues to an audio hash and distinguishes recognition-derived, provider and manual timing. Recognition and amplitude-derived estimates are not verified phoneme ground truth.

entries.title: Keeping the user's topic for follow-ups
cues: how do you use conversation history
entries.summary: A bare request to shorten or expand can preserve the prior user's topic. A substantive new question is resolved separately. The assistant's previous output cannot become evidence.

entries.title: Behavior and measured motion
entries.summary: Behavior plans carry timing and review provenance. The default planner includes demonstration rules. Measured source motion uses separate review and clock requirements and does not establish a general personality habit.

entries.title: Voice-reference validation and binding
entries.summary: The worker checks the reference audio and transcript SHA-256 digests. The studio explicitly binds the voice to the Jensen persona. A missing or mismatched reference is a configuration issue.
